questions.prompt: Every input to JavaScript `Promise.any` rejects. What result should its rejection handler receive?

sources.title: ECMAScript Language Specification: Control Abstraction Objects
sources.claim: Promise.any fulfills with the first fulfillment, but rejects with an AggregateError when all inputs reject. It does not reject at the first failed input or fulfill without a success.

questions.explanation: Promise.any fulfills with the first fulfillment, but rejects with an AggregateError when all inputs reject. It does not reject at the first failed input or fulfill without a success.

choices.text: The first rejected reason alone, because any stops on the first rejection.
An AggregateError containing the input rejection reasons.
An array of successful values, because rejected entries are silently discarded.
A fulfilled undefined value, because no input produced a usable result.

questions.prompt: A comparator uses `Intl.Collator(...).compare(a, b)`. Which assumption is portable?

sources.title: ECMAScript Internationalization API Specification
sources.claim: The comparator contract specifies negative, positive or zero according to locale-sensitive ordering, not exact -1/1 magnitude. It need not use raw code-point order; positive means a sorts after b.

questions.explanation: The comparator contract specifies negative, positive or zero according to locale-sensitive ordering, not exact -1/1 magnitude. It need not use raw code-point order; positive means a sorts after b.

choices.text: Every comparison returns exactly -1, 0 or 1 on all engines and locales.
Every comparison uses Unicode code-point order regardless of locale options.
A negative result orders a before b; its exact magnitude is not fixed.
A positive result always means the strings have the same collation order.

questions.prompt: An API receives `AbortSignal.any([userSignal, timeoutSignal])`. Which composition rules hold? Select all that apply.

sources.title: DOM Standard: AbortSignal
sources.claim: A and B: any propagates the first source abort and its reason. D: already-aborted sources are handled during construction. C describes all rather than any; E is false because source signals are not reset.

questions.explanation: A and B: any propagates the first source abort and its reason. D: already-aborted sources are handled during construction. C describes all rather than any; E is false because source signals are not reset.

choices.text: Aborting either source can abort the combined signal.
The combined signal uses the aborting source signal reason.
The combined signal waits for every source to abort before changing state.
An already-aborted input can make the combined signal aborted immediately.
Aborting a source resets other source signals to their initial state.

questions.prompt: Two inputs to `Promise.any` reject in reverse input order. In what order are their reasons listed in AggregateError.errors?

sources.title: ECMAScript Language Specification: Control Abstraction Objects
sources.claim: PerformPromiseAny records each reason at the input index. Completion timing does not reorder errors, and no alphabetical or random sorting is performed.

questions.explanation: PerformPromiseAny records each reason at the input index. Completion timing does not reorder errors, and no alphabetical or random sorting is performed.

choices.text: Rejection completion order, rather than the order of the iterable inputs.
Alphabetical order of the rejection messages, ignoring the iterable order.
Input iteration order, rather than rejection completion order.
An unspecified random order because AggregateError discards input positions.

questions.prompt: A UI sorts human names for a specific locale. Why choose Intl.Collator instead of assuming JavaScript default string ordering matches that locale?

sources.title: ECMAScript Internationalization API Specification
sources.claim: Collator is locale-sensitive and its options affect ordering. It does not translate text, always prioritize length or promise one order for every locale and sensitivity.

questions.explanation: Collator is locale-sensitive and its options affect ordering. It does not translate text, always prioritize length or promise one order for every locale and sensitivity.

choices.text: Collator converts every name to English before sorting its resulting characters.
Collator compares string lengths first and uses locale only to break equal lengths.
Collator guarantees identical ordering for every locale and every sensitivity setting.
Collator applies locale-sensitive ordering and configured collation options.

questions.prompt: Both input signals are already aborted when `AbortSignal.any([first, second])` creates a combined signal. Which statements hold? Select all that apply.

sources.title: DOM Standard: AbortSignal
sources.claim: A: construction handles already-aborted inputs immediately. B: throwIfAborted throws that signal reason. D: the algorithm selects the first already-aborted input in iteration order. C is false because reading does not reset signals; E is false because the selected source reason is preserved.

questions.explanation: A: construction handles already-aborted inputs immediately. B: throwIfAborted throws that signal reason. D: the algorithm selects the first already-aborted input in iteration order. C is false because reading does not reset signals; E is false because the selected source reason is preserved.

choices.text: The combined signal is aborted immediately.
`combined.throwIfAborted()` throws the combined signal stored reason.
Reading the combined reason resets both input signals to an active state.
The combined reason comes from the first input signal in this list.
The combined signal replaces both input reasons with a new fixed string.
